evidence: The hunk adds 'var ( ParseState = lifecycle.ParseState; ParseAction = lifecycle.ParseAction )' - package-level variables holding function values, which any importer can reassign; the reply's claim that they 'are exported functions, not variables' is contradicted by the diff it was replying to.

guidance_note: When a PR replaces a helper with a stricter one, check each call site's blank/default branch against the new helper's contract before claiming callers are safe; read + lines, not - lines.

evidence: Reply 1 planned a test confirming blank errors; reply 2 instead shipped ba8fa0a where ParseState's default branch became 'return Open, nil' for every unknown token, removing all validation. guidance_note: When the real issue is blank input, handle blank explicitly (return the zero value or default at the boundary) and keep rejecting unknown tokens; never widen a parser to accept garbage to fix an empty-string case.

evidence: Reply 2 claims the error now reads 'unknown lifecycle state %q (valid: open, in_progress, closed)', but ba8fa0a's lifecycle.go diff replaces the fmt.Errorf with 'return Open, nil' - the error was deleted, not improved.
guidance_note: Write 'Fixed' replies from the committed diff, not from the plan; quote the changed line.

evidence: The reply says ParseState 'is only called from HydrateOwnedStatus', but the PR's own hunks call model.ParseState in parseStatusFilter, statusForStorageRaw, ApplyUpdate and query applyTerm (all visible as - lines in ba8fa0a), each with a blank/'' default branch that ParseState's error made unreachable.
guidance_note: Before claiming a function has one caller, grep the branch for the call; a refactor that routes N callers through a new parser must check every one against the parser's blank-input contract.

evidence: The hunk shows '-normalized, err := normalizeStatus(status)' replaced by '+state, err := model.ParseState(status)'; the reply 'statusForStorageRaw calls normalizeStatus' again read the removed line, so import/restore with an omitted Status would have errored.
guidance_note: Same as F2: when answering a finding on a diff hunk, reason from the + lines, which are the code under review.

evidence: ba8fa0a changed statusForStorageRaw from erroring on invalid input to 'state, _ := model.ParseState(status)' that silently yields Open; the owner states import leniency is intended ('If imported data has an invalid value, it's open') and 72ac4f3 kept import on DefaultOpen, but the packet does not show whether that contract is documented anywhere.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a function from rejecting to coercing, list every caller whose error path disappears and decide per caller, in the PR, which ones are meant to be lenient.

evidence: Before ba8fa0a, 'statuses = []string{rf.Status}' passed the raw value to the store, which rejected typos; after it, 'parsed, _ := model.ParseState(rf.Status)' silently becomes open. The agent only rewrote the comment and kept ready lenient, while F9's fix made 'lit ls --status typo' error - two commands now treat the same user-typed flag differently.

evidence: ba8fa0a added parseStateSlice with 'state, _ := model.ParseState(s)' over a ParseState that now returned Open for anything, so 'lit ls --status todo' became '--status open'; 72ac4f3 made ParseState strict and propagated the error.
guidance_note: Keep validation at user-input boundaries strict and add a separately named lenient helper for stored-data paths from the start; one parser serving both roles is what F3's fix collapsed.

evidence: ba8fa0a replaced TestParseRejectsInvalidStatus with TestParseDefaultsInvalidStatusToOpen, inverting a user-visible query semantic; 72ac4f3 restored the rejection test.
guidance_note: A fix that requires inverting an existing rejection test is changing a contract; treat the inverted assertion as a stop signal, not as a test to update.

evidence: The thread's only reply is 'expected behavior', yet 25 minutes later the F9 thread announced exactly this finding's proposal - strict ParseState plus a separate DefaultOpen helper - and shipped it in 72ac4f3.
guidance_note: Resolve the root-cause thread (ParseState's contract) first and answer sibling threads from that decision, so the same suggestion is not rejected on one thread and adopted on another.

evidence: ba8fa0a made 'normalizedTarget, _ := model.ParseState(in.TargetStatus)' turn any typo into open, so 'lit update <closed-id> --status clsoed' silently reopens the issue - a data mutation, not just a missed no-op; the reply argues about consumer intent instead of the silent transition. guidance_note: For any write path, check what a typo in the input does to stored state before choosing leniency; a silent reopen of a closed issue is the case that rules it out.

evidence: ba8fa0a left parseStatusFilter returning an error it can never produce ('state, _ := model.ParseState(string(raw))'), contradicting the ListIssues boundary comment; the reply itself says 'queries should error on invalid state', which is the finding's request, then calls it 'not a real problem'.
guidance_note: When a fix makes an error return unreachable, either restore the validation or remove the error return and the comment that promises it in the same commit.

narrative: Round 0 correctly flagged that routing blank-tolerant callers through an erroring ParseState broke blank handling; the agent pushed back on F2, F5 and F6 by reading the removed lines of the hunks, and wrongly claimed F1's var aliases were functions. It then fixed the blank problem (under F3) by making ParseState coerce every unknown token to Open, which deleted input validation everywhere and produced all seven round-1 findings. Those were then resolved inconsistently across threads (F11 rejected, then its proposal adopted under F9; ready stays lenient while ls errors).
guidance_observations: Three round-0 pushbacks were built on the - side of the diff hunk; the agent should quote the + line it is defending before posting a rejection.
The fix for one finding changed a shared parser's contract without enumerating its callers, so a one-line change produced seven regressions.
Sibling threads about the same root contract were answered independently and contradicted each other; the root decision should be made once and propagated.

evidence: Assignee is a free-form string; fadb1a0 changed '--assignee <session-id>' to '--assignee <assignee>' in quickstart.md.
'if err != nil || content == "" { return "", false }' hid unreadable templates; fadb1a0 gives loadTransitionGuidance an error return and both callers propagate it.
guidance_note: Distinguish 'absent' from 'failed' at the point an optional resource is introduced; a two-value (content, ok) return that folds errors into !ok is the silent-failure shape.

guidance_note: Render each new guidance template once and run the command it prints before shipping it.

evidence: The PR deleted the quickstart embedded-template tests without replacement; fadb1a0 added TestQuickstartEmbeddedDefaultLoads. The choice to accept was right, but the new test lacked XDG_CONFIG_HOME isolation (F7).
guidance_note: When adding a test in a file whose other tests isolate env (XDG_CONFIG_HOME via t.Setenv), copy that setup.

evidence: LoadGuidance called Load(), which requires an embedded default and swallowed every error; fadb1a0 gives it its own project -> global -> optional-embedded resolver with readOptionalFile errors propagated. The new resolver then drew F8 (no tests) and F10 (path-less errors).
guidance_note: When re-implementing a sibling function's resolution logic, carry over its error format and write the same table of tests it has, in the same commit.

evidence: fadb1a0's TestQuickstartEmbeddedDefaultLoads calls Load(QuickstartTemplateName, "") with no XDG_CONFIG_HOME override, so a developer's global quickstart override decides the result; the test was deleted in 5ea19c6. The owner's second ask ('ALL tests MUST have XDG_CONFIG_HOME set globally') was answered by asserting existing tests use t.Setenv rather than by adding a package-wide guard.
guidance_note: A test written to answer a review finding gets the same isolation setup as its neighbours; check the file's existing tests for t.Setenv before writing it.

evidence: fadb1a0 introduced a three-behavior resolver (absent -> "", project/global precedence, non-ENOENT errors propagate) with no test of any branch; the reply is 'it's fine'.
guidance_note: A fix that adds a new resolver ships with a test for each branch it introduces, especially the error-propagation branch the finding asked for.

evidence: Before fadb1a0 guidance errors were swallowed, so JSON mode could not fail on them; after it, runTransition loads pre-guidance and returns 'load pre-guidance: %w' before checking isJSON, contradicting its own comment 'JSON mode bypasses guidance entirely'. The reply is 'nah'.
guidance_note: When making a previously-swallowed load fail loudly, check every mode that never used its result and skip the load there rather than adding a new failure path.

evidence: fadb1a0's errors wrap only the template name ('load guidance project template %s'), less than Load() reports; 5ea19c6 switched to the resolved path.

That fix came without tests (F8), with weaker error messages than Load (F10), and with a new failure path in JSON mode (F9); the replacement quickstart test lacked env isolation (F7). narrative: Round 0 found real bugs (swallowed writer errors, wrong init headline) that were fixed, plus an untested CLAUDE.md write that was raised three times across all rounds without ever getting a reply or a test. Rounds 1 and 2 were mostly re-raises of unanswered or not-yet-pushed round-0 findings; only F9 came from a fix, through the directory-existence heuristic for database creation. The pushback on partial two-file writes was sound.

The PR was merged with three unanswered threads (F4/F8/F11 test gap, F10 help text).

evidence: The instruction is the repo owner telling agents to run 'lit quickstart', a read-only command that prints workflow docs, before working; that is not hidden execution of anything risky. The PR was merged 8 seconds after creation, before review, and the thread was left unresolved.

narrative: A guidance-text PR merged 8 seconds after creation, before Copilot reviewed it. All three findings raise the same generic transparency concern about telling agents to run a read-only docs command without notifying the user; the premise does not hold, but the threads were never answered or resolved.
guidance_observations: Merging before the reviewer ran left three threads permanently unresolved; one pushback reply covering all three would have closed them.

evidence: The grep '"session_id":"[^"]*"' only works if the single producer (Claude Code's SessionStart stdin) emits compact JSON, which is the reply's point ('we're only trying to parse claude's json'); the packet shows neither a sample payload nor the producer's format, so whether the match is safe cannot be settled from here.
guidance_note: When matching a producer's exact output with a regex, record the producer's format (a captured sample in a comment or test) so the narrowness is a checked fact rather than an assumption.

narrative: A small hook PR with one finding about regex-based JSON extraction. The agent pushed back on the grounds that only Claude Code's own payload is parsed; the packet does not include that payload, so the pushback cannot be confirmed or refuted.
